title: Standardize ARIA phrasing and keyboard flow for compact controls — VPAT readiness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Compact controls (compact form fields, dense table rows, small action icons and inline buttons) across our component library currently have inconsistent ARIA phrasing for live updates and mixed keyboard behavior. This causes screen reader announcements to be noisy or ambiguous and creates tab-order surprises for keyboard-first users.

Goal: Create a consistent, minimal-change pattern to standardize: (1) ARIA phrasing for status/live regions and alerts, (2) keyboard flow for dense controls and segmented/action groups, and (3) token adjustments for focus and contrast to meet VPAT criteria. The end state should be VPAT-ready guidance and component updates scoped for the 2026.03 design system release.
acceptance_criteria: All compact form fields and dense table row actions use standardized aria-label/aria-describedby patterns documented in the DS spec
Roving tabindex pattern applied to segmented controls and icon-button groups where appropriate; keyboard tab order is predictable and documented
Live region usage consolidated: status updates use role=status with aria-atomic where short, assertive alerts use aria-live=assertive only when necessary
Contrast tokens for focus outlines and critical icon glyphs meet WCAG 2.1 AA (3:1 for UI components, 4.5:1 for text where applicable) and are documented
VPAT checklist updated with component-level evidence (screenshots + keystroke reproduction) and initial screening passes for NVDA/Firefox and VoiceOver/Safari
Design sign-off and engineering PRs opened with implementation notes and cross-browser test plan
design_notes: Prefer aria-describedby for multi-part labels (e.g., label + hint) to avoid screen reader truncation of the primary label
Use role=status for passive updates (e.g., autosave indicator) because it is quieter and won't interrupt forms; reserve aria-live=assertive for critical errors that require immediate attention
Implement a lightweight roving tabindex for segmented controls so only the active element is tabbable; arrow keys move focus within the group
Focus token tweak: slightly increase thickness at small densities (compact) while reducing visual footprint via inner-shadow instead of outer stroke to avoid layout shifts
Document alternative keyboard flows for dense tables: 'Enter' to open action menu + 'Esc' to return focus to the action trigger
Provide explicit example snippets for assistive tech: NVDA+Firefox, JAWS+IE (internal legacy checks), VoiceOver+Safari
implementation_steps: Audit: Inventory components with compact variant (forms, table rows, card actions, chip groups) — generate CSV of instances
Token change: propose contrast and focus token adjustments and add a migration note in tokens.md
Component updates: add aria-describedby/aria-label patterns and roving tabindex helper to segmented and icon groups
Docs: create a VPAT evidence page with annotated screenshots and keyboard scenario reproduction steps
Engineering: open feature branch + PRs, include unit tests for tabindex behavior and visual regression snapshots
QA: run targeted screen reader checklist across supported browsers and collect results
Rollout: ship as part of ds-2026.03 with a documented feature flag for edgecases and release notes
comments: 2026-02-11 — Nora Zhang: Running a quick inventory; found 78 unique compact variants across product using the old 'status' live pattern. Will attach CSV by EOD.

2026-02-18 — Aisha Kapoor: Drafted initial token proposal. Decided to increase compact focus thickness from 1px to 2px and use semi-transparent inset shadow for contrast. Posting visual samples in Figma.
2026-02-24 — Marco Reyes (Engineering): Agreed on roving tabindex approach. Suggested packaging helper as SmallRoving utility in components repo to reduce duplication. Will prototype this week.

2026-03-02 — Accessibility review (external consultant): Recommended using aria-live=polite for non-critical status updates and reserving assertive for form submission failures only. Also flagged one modal pattern that re-announces header incorrectly.

2026-03-08 — QA Lead (Priya Mehta): Performed NVDA/Firefox sweep on compact forms. Two issues: hint text being read twice when both aria-describedby and aria-live were present; and focus ring invisible at 100% zoom in Windows High Contrast. Added as bugs ENG-49802 and ENG-49803.

2026-03-12 — Nora Zhang: PRs opened: components/segmented-controls#567, components/icon-button#312, tokens/contrast#89. Linked PRs in description. Leaving some behavior behind a feature flag for experimentation. Preparing VPAT evidence page draft.
qa_plan: Create 10 keyboard-first scenario scripts (form fill, inline action, edit-in-row) and test across NVDA+Firefox, VoiceOver+Safari, and Chrome+TalkBack (Android emulation)
Record screen reader audio captures for acceptance evidence and attach to VPAT page
Cross-browser visual diff for focus states at 90%, 100%, 125% zoom and in High Contrast themes
Regression run against previous DS snapshot to ensure no unexpected visual regressions
